message.content:
Sure!  
If you want to split the string **once** at the first “=” and keep the rest of the string (including any remaining “=” characters) in the second part, just limit the number of splits:

```python
temp = "hello=good="

# Split only at the first '='
parts = temp.split('=', 1)

print(parts)          # → ['hello', 'good=']
```

`str.split(sep, maxsplit)` splits at most `maxsplit` occurrences of `sep`.  
By passing `1`, you get exactly two parts: everything before the first “=” and everything after it (which still contains the trailing “=” if present).
